examples.title: Vermilion flycatcher
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance as the camera recorded it (coarse steps).
examples.note: Wide open at about 9 m, the zone of sharpness is only 10 cm deep. A branch 3 m behind the bird spreads each point into a 1.3 mm blur on the sensor, over 40 times the sharpness limit, so the tangle behind it melts.

examples.title: Mallard and ducklings
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance as the camera recorded it (coarse steps).
examples.note: At 10 m the zone of sharpness is about 13 cm deep: enough for the ducks, not for the water behind them. Half a meter in front of focus, a point already spreads eight times wider than the sharpness limit.

examples.title: Chipmunk on a rock
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance as the camera recorded it (coarse steps).
examples.note: A distant background turns into an even wash. At these settings a point at infinity spreads into a 4 mm disk, about a ninth of the frame width, so no detail back there survives.

examples.title: Gray squirrel
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance as the camera recorded it (coarse steps).
examples.note: The closest of the long-lens shots, under 6 m away. Closer focus thins the zone of sharpness to about 4 cm, and a far background spreads to an 8 mm disk.

examples.title: Sheep above the village
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance as the camera recorded it (coarse steps).
examples.note: A 50 mm lens at f/1.8, focused near 6 m. The village far below is soft but still readable: a point that far away spreads to about 0.23 mm, where the 500 mm shots spread theirs to 4 to 8 mm.

examples.title: Sheep under the larches
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance as the camera recorded it (coarse steps).
examples.note: Focused near 6 m, the zone of sharpness runs from about 5.6 to 7.3 m. The two sheep much nearer the lens fall outside it and go soft, while the flock on the slope stays crisp.
